annotations.text:
ADO #163 — Personnel registry

Today the whole personnel model is: email, name, role, isActive, isDriver. No phone, no address, no photo, no numbers, no profile screen, and no certification concept at all.

These artboards add: profile data, four certifications (Driver / SBV / TAT / TAS) with expiry dates and scanned certificates, and a derived readiness flag.

Desk screens stay English; crew screens stay Portuguese — the app's existing rule. Full PT/EN for every screen is ADO #180.

Held vs granted

Only certifications actually awarded are stored. TAS grants TAT and SBV; TAT grants SBV. Granted ones are computed at read time and inherit the granting certificate's date — shown with a dashed border, never editable.

Where someone holds several that grant the same thing, the furthest date wins, so a lapsed TAS never masks a valid TAT.

'No expiry recorded' is its own state, in grey — never a green tick. That is what the isDriver migration writes for every existing driver.

This reverses an existing rule

Today the driver requirement is absolute — the code says so: 'The one requirement no coordinator may override: a vehicle nobody may legally drive is not cover.'

Per the PO, every requirement is now overridable, Driver included, but only with a typed reason recorded against the assignment and shown on the board and the published schedule.

A volunteer signing themselves up is still refused outright — they never see this dialog.

Day one, honestly

There is no TAT/TAS data in the database. Rosters therefore stay role-based — nothing empties — and the new Emergency defaults (Condutor→Driver, Chefe de Equipa→TAS, Socorrista→TAT) apply only to newly-opened windows, so no published schedule suddenly starts warning.

Existing drivers migrate to a Driver certification with no expiry, so the Condutor post behaves exactly as it does now.
